newsitem.title: FRANCE: No decision on French auto layoff plans - Borotra.
newsitem.headline: No decision on French auto layoff plans - Borotra.

text.p: Industry Minister Franck Borotra said in a newspaper interview that the government had not arrived at any decision regarding a request for state aid by the two big French carmakers to fund early retirement plans.
"The government has not yet made its decision," Borotra said in an interview with the newspaper Les Echos due to be published Friday. An advance copy was sent to Reuters on Thursday evening.

Borotra reiterated that the issue concerned the companies' overall competitiveness, and staff levels should not be the sole focus of efforts to help Renault and PSA Peugeot Citroen face growing competition in the years ahead.
The French carmakers, ranked fifth and sixth in January among Europe's Big Six, face greater competition when EU import quotas on Japanese vehicles are eliminated in the year 2000.

Renault and PSA Peugeot Citroen never confirmed press reports that they were seeking 40,000 job cuts, but Peugeot group chairman Jacques Calvet has said he wanted the government to foot a bigger share of the bill to finance early retirements to help the industry slim down and rejuvenate its work force.
Calvet said he would have to resort to layoffs if the government did not approve the early retirement proposal. The car companies have said that they would hire more young workers in exchange.

"Behind the question of jobs lies the problem of competitiveness of the companies. So we need to go beyond the issue of adjusting staff levels or the age pyramid to take into account overall competitiveness," Borotra was quoted as saying.

"In the event that the measures were put in place," he added, "the question of counter-actions on the part of the industrialists would come up." He did not elaborate when asked what the government was seeking in return.
But Borotra has previously said he wanted the companies to cooperate more, particularly in their drive to expand production outside Europe, to reduce their costs of doing business.
He said in the interview that any solution would have to take into account "the challenges of global competitiveness and jobs for young people."

Borotra retained industry expert Bernard Cabaret to prepare a report on the French car industry late last year after the carmakers wrote jointly to ask for assistance in financing early retirements. The Cabaret report has not been released publicly but Borotra indicated that he had seen it, and he said he had met several times with Cabaret.

Asked in the interview whether prospects for improvement in the French economy would lead to fewer layoff proposals from French companies, Borotra was vague and alluded to the pressures on companies to adapt to a rapidly evolving global environment.
France's jobless rate stands at a record 12.7 percent. (( -- Paris Newsroom, +33 1 4221 5452))
